identification: About 25 thimbles: 19 on a white ribbed porcelain three-tier thimble stand plus 6 boxed (two in a cream card box, three in small fabric-covered boxes, one in a green leather shoe-shaped case). Most are English hallmarked sterling Victorian/Edwardian/1920s-30s types with knurled crowns and band-engraved rims (Charles Horner/James Fenton/Swann/Griffiths style); hallmark cartouches visible on at least 4-5 rims, one rim appears stamped 'STERLING SILVER'. Two or three centre thimbles have darker grey crowns and may be Charles Horner Dorcas (steel-core) types; the boxed one with large square knurling looks like nickel/plate. No enamel, gold, stone-top or souvenir-topped pieces seen.

viewing_check: Count thimbles and read rims: lion passant, Chester/Birmingham anchor/sword, 'CH' (Charles Horner), 'Dorcas', 'STERLING'. Separate plated/nickel ones. Weigh the silver ones if allowed (110 g+ makes melt alone ~A$215). Check the green leather case thimble and boxed ones for gold, enamel or named pieces, and look for worn-through crowns or splits.
